Run tests as `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 8 <files>`. Tests must be hermetic (fake runner, no network, no real `claude`). Shared code must stay story-agnostic (no story, scene or character names in production code). If an OLD test pins behaviour this change deliberately changes, update it and say so in NOTES.txt. Write NOTES.txt (worktree root, never committed) listing every ambiguity and your choice. Read first: AGENTS.md and docs/contributor-guide.md. You may edit or create ONLY: factory/qualification/__init__.py, factory/qualification/run_case.py, tests/test_factory_qualification_run_case.py, tests/shard_durations.json.

TASK. Build the offline evaluation runner for the factory's diagnostic qualification (plan: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.plans/dark-factory-diagnostic-qualification-plan.md, Phase 3 'model-evaluation runner'). It runs the REAL current diagnosis and planner path on one saved case and logs everything. It never wires a patch, never calls the live narrator, never writes story files.

CASE LAYOUT (read-only input). A case directory CASE contains `solver/records.json` (shape: {"runs": [{"replicate": 1, "scene": "1A", "turns": [turn records as in a blind-player report], "stuck_turns": [turn numbers], "exit_cause": "play"|"forced"|"timer"|null}]}), `solver/repo/` (a git-archive snapshot of the story repository: `solver/repo/data/stories/<story>/...`), `manifest.json` (hashes) and `private/` (answers the runner must NEVER open). Real examples to study: /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/qual-20261122/cases/dev-1A-15d and /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/qual-20261122/cases/heldout-cand-3A.

BUILD `factory/qualification/run_case.py` with a `main(argv)` and `python -m factory.qualification.run_case` CLI: `--case-dir CASE --out OUTDIR --max-calls N --max-tokens N [--dry-run] [--story STORY_DIR_NAME]`. Behaviour:
1. REFUSE to start (exit code 2, message on stderr, nothing written) unless both --max-calls and --max-tokens are positive integers. Even --dry-run requires them (so a later billed run cannot omit them).
2. Read only files under CASE/solver and CASE/manifest.json. Never open anything under CASE/private. Convert records.json into the report shape `factory.stations.live_playtest.report_to_packets` accepts ({"replicates": [{replicate, scene, turns, stuck_turns, exit_cause}]}) and call it to get the failing-turn packets (study live_playtest._scene_runs/_turn_fails/_packet_for_turn for the exact shape; replicate must pass its validity check). Load the case's own story package from CASE/solver/repo with the same loader factory.stations.diagnose uses (`load_story_package` on the story root; see factory/stations/wiring._story_root for how the root is derived and generalise it to take an explicit repo root without changing existing behaviour; if that needs a change in wiring.py, instead add a small private helper inside run_case.py).
3. Diagnose: build a ticket (factory.tickets.Ticket, a wiring-station story_data ticket, token_budget = --max-tokens, payload with scene and failing_turns) and run `factory.stations.diagnose.diagnose_handler(...)` with `package_loader` returning the case's package and a classifier built from the real guarded path (`default_classifier`, using THIS repository's guard, ledger and caps, with its `run` argument wrapped as below). Then run the real planner `factory.stations.planner.make_planner(...)` built from this repository's guard, ledger and caps (see planner.default_planner for how they are loaded) on a ticket whose payload carries the diagnosis rows, against the case's package, with `run` wrapped as below. Use the same model ids and efforts the stations already pin; do not hardcode new ids.
4. THE CEILING WRAPPER. Wrap `subprocess.run` so every model call (an argv whose first element is `claude`) goes through a counter: before running it, if calls already made >= --max-calls or recorded tokens >= --max-tokens, raise a clear `CeilingReached` error and do NOT run it; after running it, record the call (argv, the full prompt from `input`, the full stdout and stderr, returncode, wall seconds, tokens parsed from the stream the same way planner._usage_tokens does). The runner catches CeilingReached and finishes with a result whose status is `ceiling_reached`; it never retries into a limit and never loops. Station-level LimitSleep/ProviderLimit/BudgetExhausted/ModelNotAllowed errors are caught and recorded as status `blocked` with the exception text; they are never retried or slept on.
5. Write to OUTDIR: `transcript.jsonl` (one JSON object per model call with the fields above, full text, no truncation), `packets.json`, `diagnosis.json` (rows and counts), `plan.json` (the PlanOutcome: plan or None, tokens, problems, attempts), and `result.json` with: case id (from manifest.json), the manifest's solver_tree_sha256, `git rev-parse HEAD` of the running repository if available (else null), the model ids and efforts used, ceilings, calls made, tokens, status (`complete`, `dry_run`, `ceiling_reached`, `blocked`), and the prompt texts under the exact keys `classifier_prompt` (null when no row is unclear) and `planner_prompt`. Write each file atomically (temp file then rename). Never write outside OUTDIR (the guard ledger the existing guarded_call already appends to is the one allowed exception).
6. `--dry-run`: perform steps 1-2 and the rule-only diagnosis (no classifier call), build the classifier prompt (only if some row is `unclear`) and the planner prompt exactly as the real path would build them, estimate tokens as len(prompt)//4 for each, write the same output files with status `dry_run` and the estimates in result.json, and make ZERO model calls and zero ledger writes. Print one summary line to stdout.

TESTS (new file tests/test_factory_qualification_run_case.py, hermetic, fast: whole file under 20 s; build a tiny fixture case in tmp_path from the repository's existing small test story fixtures, see how tests/test_factory_diagnose.py builds its package; do not copy the 3 MB real case). Cover: (a) refuses without ceilings and with zero/negative/non-integer values, exit 2, nothing written; (b) a fake `run` proves --max-calls 1 stops the second model call before it runs and the status is `ceiling_reached`; same for --max-tokens; (c) a fixture case with a `private/answer.json` holding a unique sentinel string: patch builtins.open and pathlib.Path.read_text/read_bytes to record every path opened during main(), then assert no recorded path is under CASE/private, and that the sentinel appears in no output file; (d) dry-run makes zero calls (fake run raises if called), writes the prompts and estimates, and leaves a temporary ledger untouched; (e) a full fake run writes all five output files, transcript lines contain the complete prompt and reply, and result.json carries the ceilings, calls, tokens and manifest hash; (f) a provider-limit error from the fake run is recorded as `blocked` and not retried (call count stays 1). Use a temporary guard allowlist, ledger and caps (see tests/test_factory_planner.py for how they build these). Then add this new test file to tests/shard_durations.json by running `.venv/bin/python scripts/regen_shard_durations.py --missing-only` (never `uv`; if the script needs network or uv, add the entry by hand with a measured duration rounded up).
Keep the module small and readable (aim under 350 lines); reuse the existing station functions instead of re-implementing diagnosis, packet building or planning.

set -eo pipefail
WORK=/home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/factory-21
mkdir -p "$WORK/out"
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp
[ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv
git add -A -- factory tests
bad=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -vE '^(factory/qualification/__init__\.py|factory/qualification/run_case\.py|tests/test_factory_qualification_run_case\.py|tests/shard_durations\.json)$' || true)
[ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "files outside ownership staged: $bad"; exit 1; }
start=$(date +%s)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 8 tests/test_factory_qualification_run_case.py tests/test_factory_diagnose.py tests/test_factory_planner.py tests/test_factory_live_playtest.py
took=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))
echo "tests took $took s (budget 300 s)"
[ "$took" -le 300 ] || { echo "over the 300 s budget"; exit 1; }
PYFILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep '\.py$' || true)
[ -z "$PYFILES" ] || .venv/bin/python -m ruff check $PYFILES
[ -z "$PYFILES" ] || .venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check $PYFILES
FAKE=$WORK/out/fakebin
mkdir -p "$FAKE"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "a model was called" >&2\nexit 99\n' > "$FAKE/claude"
chmod +x "$FAKE/claude"
for CASE in dev-1A-15d heldout-cand-3A; do
  OUT="$WORK/out/dry-$CASE"
  rm -rf "$OUT"
  if PATH="$FAKE:$PATH" .venv/bin/python -m factory.qualification.run_case --case-dir /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/qual-20261122/cases/$CASE --out "$OUT" --max-calls 5 --max-tokens 100000 --dry-run; then :; else echo "dry run failed on $CASE"; exit 1; fi
  .venv/bin/python - "$OUT" <<'PYV'
import json, sys
from pathlib import Path
out = Path(sys.argv[1])
result = json.loads((out / "result.json").read_text())
assert result["status"] == "dry_run", result["status"]
assert result["calls"] == 0, "dry run made a call"
packets = json.loads((out / "packets.json").read_text())
assert packets, "no failing-turn packets built from the case"
assert isinstance(result.get("planner_prompt"), str) and result["planner_prompt"], "planner prompt missing"
assert "classifier_prompt" in result, "classifier_prompt key missing"
transcript = out / "transcript.jsonl"
assert not transcript.exists() or transcript.read_text().strip() == "", "dry run wrote model calls"
print(out.name, "packets", len(packets), "ok")
PYV
done
if .venv/bin/python -m factory.qualification.run_case --case-dir /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/qual-20261122/cases/dev-1A-15d --out "$WORK/out/noceiling" --dry-run 2>/dev/null; then echo "runner started without ceilings"; exit 1; fi
test ! -e "$WORK/out/noceiling" || { echo "refusal wrote output"; exit 1; }
git diff --cached > "$WORK/out/qualification-runner.patch"
test -s "$WORK/out/qualification-runner.patch"
tasks.verified: A dry run on two real cases builds packets and prompts with zero model calls; ceilings are mandatory; private/ is never read.
